text:
Juraj Slafkovsky has 2 goals in 23 games and none in his last 14, which looks like a slump until you look at the chances. He has 8.3 expected goals (the quality of his shots), and he's shooting 3.8% against a league norm of 13.3%. Our numbers flag him as due: he keeps getting the looks.

The rest of his game is holding. He has 12 assists, plays 18.4 minutes a night, and Montreal breaks about even at five on five with him on the ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 88th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, so the passing is a real skill and not a fluke.

The fair concern sits on the other side of the puck. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.17 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 7% of forwards, while he faced the other team's best. He's 22, the first overall pick of 2022, and fresh off 8 points at the Olympics for Slovakia. The finishing should come back.
headline: Slafkovsky is getting chances; the puck won't go in
